question: Should outbound recovery keep ambiguous rows pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed after the recovery pass?
rationale: The code defect can be repaired mechanically, but the steady-state choice between recoverable pending rows and clearer terminal failed rows is an operator/product behavior decision that tests alone cannot settle.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending After Repair
options.body: Merge after the no-op pacing bug is fixed and exact-head validation is green if maintainers want ambiguous rows preserved for later adapter reconciliation.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the broader delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a companion doctor, UI, or API surface before changing ambiguous rows to remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending After Repair
recommendation.body: Merge after the no-op pacing bug is fixed and exact-head validation is green if maintainers want ambiguous rows preserved for later adapter reconciliation.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses core queue semantics, SQLite-backed recovery state, and operator behavior where this owner has recent co-author and migration history.
